body: **2026-10-10-viola-revive** — put `revive` among the CLI verbs and made a passed revive enter the TUI passthrough boundary (contract/tui-passthrough/entry, decision/single-vendor-content-boundary). The revive refusal is a fixed-message `unable:` line with `hint:` last, and while the child holds the terminal a passed revive writes no line of its own. `viola up` re-opens each instance through this revive path, so every start it makes is bound by that boundary, and up's own per-instance lines must never reach a terminal a child already holds.

**2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board** — revive's preflight makes one `claude agents --json` read with a 5 s kill, and the read fails open (decision/claude-agents-read-fails-open). The bound falls on viola's own child, never on the human. When up runs revive's preflight once per instance, that read repeats N times, which bears on the wall-time premise. The fail-open rule stays: a failed read passes revive.

**2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract** — gave revive `--json` on both arms: each exit-1 refusal is one `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` document with empty stderr, and the human pair stays byte-identical. This is the precedent for the `--json` form of up's per-instance outcomes (contract/revive-json-refusal/document). The document carries codes only, with no hint.

**2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline** — built the `--help` group labels over the served verbs only, and the colour decision (NO_COLOR, TERM, COLORTERM, TTY; no SGR under `--json`), with each SGR span beside its word. A new human verb `up` needs a row in a help group (contract/cli-help/group-labels, served-verbs-only, usage-line), pinned by `help_is_the_grouped_verb_table` and `help_lists_only_served_verbs`. Any styling of up's outcome words must follow decision/no-sgr-off-terminal and decision/word-beside-every-sgr.
**2026-10-20T06-58-31-wrap** — the founder ratified that `--help` rows cover the served verbs only, removing the PROVISIONAL mark. Adding `up` to a help group follows this standing rule.

**2026-10-26-explicit-session-links** (the `handoff:` help row built) — the precedent for a new verb's help row: `handoff:  link, unlink` was placed between `wheel:` and `setup:` and pinned by the two help cases. `up` will change the same pinned table (contract/cli-help/group-labels), and the group labels serve as terminal structural equivalents (decision/terminal-structural-equivalents).

**2026-10-26-explicit-session-links** (the link verbs' result lines among the literal-pinned strings) — each result line is one write with no SGR and is pinned by literal. Names printed in result lines are the verb's own parsed arguments, never names read back from a reply or the log (decision/printed-names-are-parsed-arguments). Up's one line per instance names an instance it read from the board rather than from argv, so this rule's reach needs a decision, and up's fixed lines take a literal pin.

**2026-10-26-home-and-code-bearing-file-integrity** — `run`, a revive start and `verify` refuse a home tree that fails the strict-modes check: exit 1 before any log opens, the home-state pair on stderr with `hint:` last, and no child (contract/start-refusal/home-strict-modes, decision/strict-modes-refusal-before-any-write). Up must decide whether it checks the home once before any start or relays each revive start's refusal.

**2026-10-31-sanitised-error-surfaces** — `--json` failures are each one clean document: a literal exit, empty stderr, no ESC byte, and no path or upstream text (decision/json-failure-documents-are-clean). The `answer` and `send` exit-2 paths are the exception (decision/json-one-document-no-hint). Peer replies are screened to code words (decision/peer-replies-screened-to-code-words), and the census of error writers holds each error body to a writer and a witness. Up's `--json` outcome document must hold codes and closed words only and join the census.

**2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue** — `viola revive --json` gives one exit-1 document for every refusal of the start it shares with `run` (contract/viola-revive-json/start-refusal). A `pump_child` error prints no document because the child has held the terminal. Exit 1 separates a stale holder (`stale-heartbeat`) from a live one (`already-live`) (contract/start-holder-refusal/*). The entry also added `no_two_codes_share_a_hint`, `no_hint_names_release` and the exit-cause table in `tests/cross_exit_causes.rs`. Up's skip of live instances and its relay of revive's closed codes rest on these, and any new code or hint must pass the one-hint-per-code and no-release guards.

**2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue** (the `cli` catch site's `internal-error` document) — where a verb prints `error: internal error`, under `--json` it prints the internal-error document instead. `run` and revive's start stay silent there (contract/json-fault/internal-error). Up must say which of these forms its own catch site takes, given that each start it makes is silent.

**2026-11-01-unix-endpoint-and-home-hardening** — a refused socket directory at a `run` or revive start gives exit 1 before any snapshot, bind or child, in the fixed-message pair form. Under `revive --json` it gives the one `socket-dir-refused` document, which holds no path, pid or uid (contract/start-refusal/socket-dir, contract/revive-json-refusal/socket-dir-refused, decision/socket-dir-refusal-before-any-frame). Every start up makes can meet this refusal, and up's per-instance line must not leak a path.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** — set the closed set of revive `--json` exit-1 codes at ten, with `batch-script-child` gone. It also set the Linux-only platform line (core, ubuntu-latest CI, the 0.2.0 window features on Hyprland; decision/linux-only), made the manual pass Orca alone (GNOME Terminal for cli, foot on Hyprland for tui; nothing gated on it), and moved the a11y cases to the one ubuntu-latest `coverage` leg. Up's outcomes relay that closed code set. Its window placement is Hyprland-only, and its tests run on ubuntu-latest.

**2026-11-06-version-done-check** — moved the cli output-discipline checks to `std::process::Command` with literal pins, which replaced trycmd and assert_cmd (decision/fixed-cli-strings-pinned, decision/refusal-layout-literal-pins, decision/cli-a11y-by-literal-tests). Up's fixed strings, its outcome lines and its refusal layout are pinned the same way, and a copy change fails CI.

**2026-11-08T20-32-52-wrap** — retired the frontend stubs to N/A: viola has no web or graphical frontend, and the terminal fleet console takes its keyboard a11y scope at «Fleet a11y verification». This explains the N/A rows the picked set holds for §5–§7. `up` stays a cli surface and is not a console entry.

**2026-11-14-budget-gate-removed** — retired exit 11 (budget-paused), never to be reused (contract/cli-exit-codes/11), and dropped the budget pause from both time-bound lists. Up must not take exit 11. This entry is also part of the record of how the time-bound lists have been edited.

**2026-11-14-status-line-interception-removed** — dropped the statusline deadline from decision/time-bounds-never-on-human and decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver. These are the two time-bound lists that the scope says will not grow for up.

**2026-11-18-session-folder-trusted-by-viola** — the start's trust step reports its outcome in one `trust-record` line in `diagnostics/`, never as a refusal, exit code or hint (decision/run-diagnostics-off-terminal). A wrapped TUI in an untrusted folder opens on its session box (decision/wrapped-tui-reads-as-unwrapped except). The start's Claude config lock wait joined both time-bound lists as a bound on viola's own start. Each revive start that up makes runs this trust step and lock wait, which adds to wall time across N starts and does not fall on the human.

**2026-11-20-a-new-cli-version-stamped-automatically** — a keyed start's automatic verify window comes before the child, and its lines L1–L5 and verify's own output come before the child's bytes. This window is the one exception to never-blocked keys (contract/tui-passthrough/human-keystrokes, contract/tui-passthrough/viola-terminal-bytes, decision/human-keystrokes-never-blocked). Ratified at 2026-11-22T17-29-41Z. Each start that up makes may enter this window, so up's own lines must not interleave with it.

**2026-11-21-mcp-calls-bounded** — added the MCP call deadline to both time-bound lists and `call-deadline` as an unreachable cause. It is the latest growth of the two lists before they reached full. Up is CLI-only with no MCP tool, per the scope's conservative arm, so no MCP bound applies.

**2026-11-22-paste-write-bounded** — changed the delay bound on a human key to the paste's in-flight chunk and closing marker (contract/tui-passthrough/human-keystrokes, decision/human-keystrokes-never-blocked). Each passthrough that up opens through revive inherits this promise as it now reads.

**2026-11-22T17-29-41Z-wrap** — gave contract/tui-passthrough/own-bytes, decision/zero-viola-bytes-on-the-terminal, decision/wheel-ignores-terminal-events and decision/portable-pty-outer-pty-driver the automatic-verify exception. It also added paste write to both time-bound lists, which left them full at their bound. Up's starts sit inside these boundary rows, and the scope's full time-bound list cell comes from this entry.

**2026-11-22-epoch-4-cleanup** — because the two time-bound lists are full, the operator ruled that a new time bound lands as a row of its own: decision/start-verify-stop-grace-off-the-human. This is the precedent for any bound up adds, such as a fleet-wide or per-start wait. Under the scope, that row waits on fork F1 of run `2026-11-24T00-26-24Z-wrap` and is listed in Expected amendments.

**2026-11-22-lineage-registry** — the board draws wrapped rows as a tree with a plain-space NAME indent and a `-- LINKS --` block (decision/terminal-structural-equivalents, decision/cli-structural-landmark-equivalents). Up orders parents before children by this lineage record. If up's per-instance lines show depth, they must use the same plain-space indent and no other structure carrier.

**2026-11-23-viola-open-2** — `viola open` added an exit-2 refusal that is one fixed stderr line with no document and echoes none of the refused words (contract/cli-exit-codes/2). It is now among the `--json` exceptions (decision/json-one-document-no-hint, contract/cli-refusal/json). Up opens each window the way `open` would, so any usage path it adds must either fit exit 2 as a clap usage error or extend this exception list by name.

**2026-11-24-viola-focus** — the precedent for a non-frame verb: `focus` joined the exit-21 strict-modes list and contract/cli-exit-codes/21 for refusals before any compositor read. Both remain PROVISIONAL (delegate, fork F-A). If up refuses an instance or home before any Hyprland read, these rows would have to name up the same way. Up's rows rest on a provisional base.

Adds a new human CLI verb `viola up` that re-opens the fleet after a host reboot: it reads the board's instances under the home, selects those that were live before the host went down, and orders them parents before children by the recorded lineage.
It skips every instance whose recorded pid and start time verify live, and re-opens each remaining one resumed in place through the existing `revive` start arm, in the terminal window `viola open` would give it, in its recorded workspace.
It prints one line per instance naming the instance and a closed outcome word, and under `--json` one document of codes and closed words only, beside the existing CLI machine contract.
It adds tests proving the selection, order, skip, lines and the argv handed to each start over the fake agent and the Hyprland fakes under a test-owned home; every live reading of `up` is left to the operator and its clause GATED.

body: The new verb joins the CLI verb table and `viola --help`: its help row, its group label, the usage line, and only served verbs listed; it is a human CLI verb only, with no MCP tool added (the driver re-opening the fleet stays CLI-only).

Each per-instance line is linear, static, plain output: one line per instance written whole, no spinner or progress redraw while a fleet of N starts, a closed outcome word carrying the state in print rather than by colour.

Colour on the up lines: no SGR when stdout is not a colour-capable terminal, any SGR only beside its word, refusal and failure words never coloured, and the colour decision taken from the same inputs as the other verbs.

Instance names, workspaces or any other recorded value printed on an up line or a refusal pass through C0/C1 control-character escaping; printed names are the instance names, never paths (paths not carried).
Under `--json`, `up` emits one clean document of codes and closed words only, no hint, no SGR, no free text; failure documents and fault bodies under `--json` keep the CLI machine contract's shape.

An instance the `revive` start arm refuses yields its existing closed refusal code (already-live, session-live, stale-heartbeat, cwd-missing, no-session, squatted-name, pinned-hash-mismatch, strict-modes-failed, socket-dir-refused, internal-error) on that instance's line or in the `--json` document; unlisted code words stay visible, never swallowed or renamed.

Human refusals of `up` itself keep the CLI refusal form: an unable line with its kebab-case reason code beside a plain word, then exactly one hint line per code, faults and the `unknown` refusal carrying no hint, no hint naming a release, no stack trace or bare status as the error text, and thiserror messages interpolating nothing.

Exit codes of `up` come from the existing CLI exit-code table (usage error 2, refusal 1, the existing higher codes for unreachable or failed instances); a fleet with some instances refused or skipped maps to a stated code, never a new undeclared one.
Home strict-modes and socket-directory checks run before any write or any frame: an unstattable or loose home is a strict-modes refusal, and a socket-directory failure refuses before the first start.
The skip of a still-live instance reads the board's liveness (snapshot pid plus start time, heartbeat) and is reported as its own closed outcome word on that instance's line.
Each re-open goes through `revive`'s preflight, including the `claude agents --json` read, which fails open as it does for a single revive; `up` adds no stricter gate of its own on that read.

Time bounds of each start (start verification, its stop grace, the wait for a parent before its children) fall on the driver, never on the human: no time limit is put on the operator and no timeout ends silently.
`up` asks nothing interactively: no prompt, no confirmation, no keyboard input read from the operator while it runs.

Each re-opened session runs inside the `viola run` TUI passthrough in its own terminal window: zero viola bytes on that terminal, the terminal belongs to the child, human keystrokes are never blocked, and run diagnostics never reach the terminal; `up` writes nothing into a child's terminal.
The per-instance process-log line keeps the NEVER-log floor (no window address, pid or workspace in a process-log line) and carries the log identity tags (process, service_name).
The fixed strings of `up` (outcome words, line layout, refusal and hint copy) come from design and are pinned by literal in tests, the refusal layout held by literal pins.

Live readings of `up` (a real host restart, a real resumed session, a real window) never gate the build; the fakes carry what they can and the rest is GATED on the operator's reading, with manual keyboard or screen-reader passes supplemental only.

body: The `viola list` board rows (caption order, empty board, unwrapped separator, stale-row dim, NAME bold and truncation): `up` prints its own per-instance lines, not the board.

Dialog, send, answer and wheel rows (dialog amber, dialog hold, dialog-expired event, send refusals while the human types, human key takes the wheel, MCP wait tool timeout): `up` neither answers dialogs nor sends prompts.
MCP server frame-tool and hook event or dialog-call rows: `up` adds no MCP tool and no hook call.
`viola link` / `viola unlink`, `viola plugin install`, `viola verify` and `viola wait` / `last` output contracts: other verbs whose lines `up` does not write.

Absences and graphical-frontend rows (web or graphical frontend, touch surface, rendered page, internationalization) and the empty WCAG-criteria, contrast and focus-management harness areas: `up` is a terminal CLI verb.

Tier, compliance-regime and conformance-claim decisions (a11y tier Standard, no WCAG conformance claim, no compliance regime, cognitive accessibility not triggered): plan-level settings the chunk does not change.

**2026-09-27-instance-state-and-start-order** — tempfile `persist` snapshot writer, liveness by process check, start order as landed: pid + start time decide `gone` whatever the beat; same process → `live` (≤ 5 s beat) or `stale`; a `live`/`stale` name refuses `already-live`, a `gone` one is taken over at once. Origin of the live/stale/gone reading `viola up` uses to select and skip instances (decision/liveness-heartbeat-and-pid, decision/session-liveness-heartbeat-and-start-time).

**2026-10-10-viola-revive** (the `revive` verb registered: subcommand, exit-1 refusals, child flags, log producer) — `revive <name> [--id] [--fork] [-- <child args>]` / `--list`, sends no channel frame, preflight refusals exit 1, the child launched by name on PATH with `--plugin-dir` first and `--resume <id>` (newest logged id); `run-<name>.ndjson` has revive's start arm as second producer. The per-instance path `up` re-uses for each re-open.

**2026-10-10-viola-revive** (the snapshot's `cwd` and the child's second cwd source) — the snapshot gains `cwd?`; a revived start spawns in the recorded `cwd`, read only after the strict-modes check and required to exist, else `cwd-missing`; a replayed snapshot gives no cwd, so revive over it is refused. Founder-ratified widening; bears on which instances `up` can actually re-open after a reboot (contract/instance-snapshot/cwd, decision/revive-refused-without-cwd, decision/child-cwd-explicit).

**2026-10-10-viola-revive** (the replay's first product reader, the session chain, revive as the second way a wrapper starts) — revive refuses a `live`/`stale` name through the same collision check (run twice: preflight and start), resumes the `gone` instance in place appending to `events.ndjson`, replays no launch, first record `wheel{holder:"driver", cause:"start"}` (founder's answer). `replay::session_chain` gives the logged session ids `up` would resume.

**2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through** (four crossings ratified by the founder) — the logged session id as the value of `--resume` on a revived child's command line reads as ratified (decision/logged-session-id-on-child-argv). `up` puts that same crossing on N children at once; no new crossing unless `up` adds one.

**2026-10-10-budget-governor** (the instance check before any log, on both arms) — revive's start arm runs `check_instance` before its wrapper log opens, because opening a log narrows an existing home to 0700 and a later check passes a 0770 home; a refusal writes no line. Trap for `up`: any per-instance log line it writes must come after each instance's check (decision/strict-check-before-log-open, decision/instance-check-before-any-read).

**2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list** — `list` is a caller-side board (`board::scan` then `board::read`), contacts no wrapper; the replay fallback gives `live` for a replayed snapshot only with a beat ≤ `STALE_AFTER`, never `stale`; a failed check on the home, `instances/` or any instance refuses the whole board, exit 21, no log, no line. The board read model `up` reads its candidates from (decision/list-is-caller-side-read, decision/board-refused-whole, decision/replayed-snapshot-liveness).

**2026-10-13-t06-38-35-wrap** — the founder's Epoch 4 batch: `viola list`'s whole-board exit-21 refusal with no log and no line is his own ruling (decision/board-refused-whole); precedent for whether `up` refuses the whole fleet on one refused instance or skips it.

**2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board** (Standard Contracts: the agents read, the join and the unwrapped rack land) — `list`, revive's preflight and verify spawn one bounded `claude agents --json` read (`run::agents`, R8 strip, `MAX_FRAME` cap, 5 s kill), joined by `child_pid` / `agent_session_id`; a failed read degrades, never errors. `up`'s skip/selection must not depend on it (decision/agents-listing-never-errors, decision/agents-join-read-ungated, decision/process-liveness-signals).

**2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board** (Session Liveness: revive refuses a session id live elsewhere) — revive's preflight gains `session-live`: a `claude agents --json` row holding the logged id refuses (two writers on one transcript measured), `--fork` skips it, a failed read passes (fail open). Each revive `up` drives runs this read (decision/revive-refuses-live-session, contract/viola-revive-json-error-codes/session-live).

**2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract** (revive takes --json on both arms; revive --list is a cli producer) — revive `--json` prints `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` for its refusals, codes only; without `--json` the human pairs byte-identical; `role_of` files `revive --list` under `cli`. The machine contract `up --json` sits beside (decision/cli-human-text-json-exit-codes, decision/cli-output-conventions).

**2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract** (the CLI verbs take the VIOLA_DIR step and canonicalise the home) — `resolve_home`: `--home`, else the `VIOLA_DIR` grandparent when `VIOLA_NAME`+`VIOLA_DIR` pass the shape check, else `<user home>/.viola`; `canonical_home`. Ratified later at 2026-10-18-plugin-precedence-live-readings. `up`'s home and what it hands each re-opened child follow this rule (decision/session-home-from-viola-dir, decision/viola-home-resolution).

**2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline** — the colour layer reads `NO_COLOR` / `TERM` / `COLORTERM`, never sets or echoes them; they decide only SGR bytes; any further environment read needs its own ratification (decision/colour-env-decides-only-sgr, decision/clap-without-color-feature). Binds `up`'s one human line per instance.

**2026-10-26-server-verification-before-any-frame** (the snapshot's pid and started_at as the server identity every frame-writing client checks) — `live_endpoint` returns `LiveEndpoint {endpoint, pid, started_at}` from one snapshot read; `server_verdict` compares pid and OS start time in whole seconds through sysinfo, a zombie reading gone. The mechanism behind «pid-and-start-verified live ones skipped» (decision/server-start-time-read-through-sysinfo, contract/instance-snapshot/pid-and-started-at, contract/instance-snapshot/started-at).

**2026-10-26-home-and-code-bearing-file-integrity** (the snapshot readers moved onto the replay) — every product snapshot reader goes through `read_snapshot_or_replay`; a replayed snapshot carries no `endpoint`, `pid` or `started_at`, so the collision check judges liveness from the heartbeat alone (decision/snapshots-read-through-replay, decision/replayed-snapshot-gives-no-live-endpoint). After a reboot `up` must read the fleet through this path.

**2026-10-26-home-and-code-bearing-file-integrity** (what each replay reader decides; one read per revive, one state-recovered line) — a replayed snapshot writes one `state-recovered` line into the reading process's role file per replay; revive reads the snapshot once for its holder check and recorded directory. Trap: `up` reading each snapshot and then revive reading it again doubles the replay and its line (decision/revive-reads-snapshot-once, decision/replay-writes-no-file, contract/diag-line/state-recovered).

**2026-10-26-home-and-code-bearing-file-integrity** (the home-tree check before the start's and verify's log; the pin key taken once) — `check_home_tree` runs at every start before its wrapper log via `checked_exe`; a refusal is exit 1, no log, no line, no child; `run` pins the very bytes its check hashed (decision/start-pins-the-bytes-it-checked, contract/run-start-refusals/home-tree).

**2026-10-26-home-and-code-bearing-file-integrity** (the checked entry points and check_instance's call sites; viola list's two home checks) — every checked entry point runs its strict-modes or instance check ahead of any log, a refusal writing no line, the mode left as found; `check_instance(` call sites counted under `src/`. A new verb like `up` joins this list (decision/strict-modes-check-before-log, decision/refused-check-writes-no-line).

**2026-10-27-pinned-copy-race-and-reproducible-builds** (the pinned copy on disk: placed once with no clobber) — two concurrent first starts raced the pinned copy (ETXTBSY 4/24); now `place_private_new` no-clobber, a lost placement re-hashes the copy that stands. Precedent for `up` launching several starts at once (decision/pinned-binary-copy, decision/pinned-copy-rehash).

**2026-10-31-sanitised-error-surfaces** (the sanitised error surfaces pattern and its contract binary) — CLI `--json` documents carry codes and fixed messages only, no path, pid or upstream text; `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs` census enumerates every error body. `up --json` must be codes and closed words only and land its rows in that census (decision/sanitised-error-surfaces).

**2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue** (`stale-heartbeat`, a stale holder's own code) — run's collision refusal is `already-live` for a live holder or fresh replayed beat and `stale-heartbeat` for a stale holder; revive's first preflight reading likewise. The codes an `up` per-instance skip/refusal outcome would surface (contract/viola-revive-json-error-codes/stale-heartbeat, contract/process-exit-detail/stale-heartbeat).

**2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue** (`viola revive --json` documents every refusal of its start) — `Launch.json` makes refusals after a passed preflight print the refused document; a program not found prints `internal-error`; a `pump_child` error prints no document because the child has held the terminal (decision/no-document-after-child-held-terminal, contract/revive-json/*).

**2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue** (the `cli` catch site's `internal-error` document) — a `cli` verb with `--json` before a `--` prints `{"v":1,"error":"internal-error","detail":null}` at the catch site; run, revive's start, mcp and hook stay silent there (decision/silent-roles-at-internal-error-catch, contract/cli-json-output/internal-error).

**2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue** (`without_endpoint`, the no-endpoint reading) — with no live endpoint the instance directory is read: a directory is `instance-dead`, anything else `unwrapped-name`; `live_endpoint` gives none for a stale wrapper. Reading a dead wrapper without opening anything, as `up`'s selection needs.

**2026-11-01-unix-endpoint-and-home-hardening** (the start's refused socket directory, exit 1) — `socket_dir_ready` before any snapshot, child or bind; a failed create and a refused check both read `socket-dir-refused`, a bind failure does not (decision/socket-dir-refused-covers-create-and-check, contract/run-start-refusals/socket-dir-refused). After a reboot the runtime socket dir is gone and is re-made by each start.

body: A new CLI verb in the verb table, help rows, exit-cause tables and exit codes, and its --json machine contract: an error document and output of codes and closed words only, beside the existing CLI machine contract.
The verb is CLI-only: a driver session re-opening the fleet is a boundary widening, held to its conservative arm, so no agent-facing tool is added for it.

CLI input handling for the new verb: its flags and home selection (--home, VIOLA_DIR, the CLI home resolution order) checked before anything is read, and any instance name passed through the validated name type.

The board read model: the home and state tree pass the strict-modes check before any read, the board scan refuses a readable home and refuses the whole board, readers are bounded, tolerate torn lines and never write.

Snapshot values (recorded cwd, workspace, placement, lineage, launch pair, window and origin) are used only after the strict-modes check, only when they re-parse, and a replayed snapshot stays inert; the recorded cwd is used only to spawn.

The parent-before-child order comes from the self-reported lineage record, which authenticates nothing; a missing, never-live or cyclic parent must not let a recorded value become a command or a target.
Liveness skip: an instance is skipped only when its recorded pid and process start time verify live through the process-identity reading, with the heartbeat as the board's other liveness signal.

Each re-open goes through revive's existing start arm with its preflight (the claude agents read, session-live), its strict-modes checks, socket-directory check before bind, start collision check (already-live, stale-heartbeat) and closed revive refusal codes, which up must carry as closed words, never as upstream text.

The argv handed to each start: session id as one argv element of a closed shape, the launch pair on the claude child's argv, no shell, the claude program resolved from PATH, the pinned binary re-hashed before reuse.
The child environment at each start: parent identity variables (no inherited VIOLA_* name) and inherited CLAUDE credentials stripped from the child.

The terminal window per instance through viola open's path: the terminal spawned directly with its closed argument allowlist, the wrapper's window record under --origin, the recorded window origin authenticating nothing, and the wrapper's window step moving only its own terminal's window.

The Hyprland seam: only its closed request set, hyprctl children bounded by a deadline, Hyprland reply text dropped at the parse; a recorded window address dies with the compositor and is never trusted after a reboot.
Lineage, launch pair and window records stay kept to the snapshot and the event log at every start.

The per-instance outcome line in human mode: C0/C1 controls escaped, no paths, pids, ids, addresses or workspaces in a refusal or error line, error messages that interpolate nothing and carry no upstream text.
The obs event catalog gains a per-instance line for up, under the never-log floor: no address, pid or workspace in a process-log line, full error detail only in diagnostics.
Nothing written or read under the operator's Claude home: viola writes nothing under the Claude home, and this phase reads nothing of the real ~/.claude* trees.

No live act in this phase: no live start, no window opened, moved, focused or closed, no Hyprland dispatch, no key sent, no real session revived, no list against the real claude on PATH; every live reading of up is gated on the operator at the host.
The new tests prove selection, order, skip, lines and the argv of each start over the fake agent and the Hyprland fakes, with the real claude CLI only local and never in CI.

every new error writer is named and uses fixed display messages that interpolate nothing
CI holds no secrets and runs no real claude CLI; new CI tests run over the fakes only

An unbounded one hung 27 minutes. `up`'s remove-the-guard controls start processes, so their witnesses must be bounded.

Adds a new human CLI verb `viola up`: the fleet re-opened after a reboot, consuming only normalised state and events.
It scans the board's instances under the home, selects those that read as live before the host went down, orders them parents before children by the recorded lineage, skips every one whose recorded pid and start time verify live, and re-opens each remaining one resumed in place through the existing revive start path, in the terminal window viola open would give it, in its recorded workspace.
It prints one line per instance naming the instance and a closed outcome word, and under --json one document of codes and closed words only.
It adds the tests that prove the selection, the order, the skip, the lines and the argv handed to each start, over the fake agent and the Hyprland fakes under a test-owned user home; it re-measures at HEAD the lineage and launch lines at every start, viola open's window and its window record under --origin, and revive resuming in place.

body: A new CLI verb joins the verb table: the grouped verb table of viola --help, its help row, its exit codes and exit causes, each exit cause with its own hint; help carries no bold or underline.

Under --json the verb prints exactly one JSON document per run on stdout, of codes and closed words only, beside the existing CLI --json success and failure document shapes; error bodies hold no path or upstream text.

One human line per instance naming the instance and a closed outcome word: instance names escaped (every control character shown, never raw), no escape or SGR bytes without a terminal, human output pinned by literal asserts in the tests; an unknown refusal word stays visible.

The board read model: the board scan of instances under the home, the snapshot read through read-or-replay (a broken snapshot replayed from the event log, the replay writing no file and carrying no endpoint or cwd), the tolerant event log reader that counts and skips unknown or torn lines, and tailing that ignores symlinks and invalid names; the board held to the home read rule.

The skip of a live instance: instance liveness live, stale and gone, read from the snapshot pid plus start time and the heartbeat; heartbeat staleness classification by age and by pid or start-time mismatch, through the pure classifier that takes its instant; a pid reused by another process is never read live.

The selection of what was live before the host went down versus what ended on purpose, read from snapshot, heartbeat and event log; runtime-dir sockets and locks may not survive a reboot (the endpoint is read only from the snapshot and a gone endpoint is not liveness).

Parents before children: the order is taken from the recorded lineage line {parent, role} of each start; a missing, never-live or cyclic parent must still yield one outcome line per instance and never hang or panic.

Each re-open goes through revive's start arm: its preflight order (the agents list via claude agents --json, the session-live reading that fails open, the agents list that reads unknown when unreadable), and its closed refusal codes (already-live, session-live, no-session, cwd-missing, stale-heartbeat, squatted-name, socket-dir-refused, pinned-hash-mismatch, strict-modes-failed, internal-error), each surfacing as that instance's outcome rather than ending the fleet run.

Revive's exit codes and exit 1 causes, its human refusal line and its --json refusal document, as the outcome `up` reads per instance and maps to its own closed words; no revive document once a child holds the terminal.

Strict-modes checks on the home tree before any read or open: a home readable by another user refused, a widened home tree refused, the socket directory checked and refused, never repaired or chmod-ed; the strict-modes refusal exit and its per-verb rows apply to the new verb.

The terminal window each re-open gets is viola open's terminal spawn, and the wrapper's window record {address, workspace, placement, origin} under --origin; the Hyprland seam's closed request set is used, never widened; a recorded compositor address does not survive a reboot.

Real window placement and every clause needing a real host restart or a real resumed session are proven only by a gated live reading the operator grants; the live reading is recorded as a reading, never as verification, and a fake-agent run is no proof of real-CLI behaviour.
Every start the verb makes records the launch pair {model, effort} and the lineage line {parent, role}; these are re-measured at HEAD in the new tests, not copied.

The started child's environment: the CLAUDE* environment strip, the child given its viola name, instance dir and binary, and holding nothing else of viola's; its process-start record of env kept and stripped counts.

The argv handed to each start is asserted through the fake agent's command line and receipt (argv, cwd, env, start), the fake agent configured by argv alone and placed on a test-scoped PATH; the Hyprland side through real stub executables on PATH.

A per-instance obs event in the event catalog: a process log line in structured JSON per line with its event, instance and corr fields, codes only with detail apart; the NEVER-log floor holds: no address, pid or workspace in a process-log line, no secret in logs or diagnostics.
CLI-only, no MCP tool: the MCP tools/list tool set is unchanged and there is no control tool over MCP; re-opening the fleet is never reachable from a driver session's MCP surface.

Tests run viola as a subprocess under a test-owned user home and runtime dir: test-started viola drops inherited env and session variables, every spawned viola and wrapper is tied (drop guard, tied spawn thread), and tests never read the host's claude sessions or the real claude CLI.

Waits in the new tests key on logged events with bounded waits inside the existing wait bounds (the WITHIN bound, root waits below the kill lines, the per-test kill for stamped-home tests); no new time bound is added while its fork waits.

Revive's resume in place and the start events' order (run start events, the first wheel record of a start, child spawn after events) as the existing start path gives them, re-measured at HEAD for a revived instance.

body_fields.convention: each new root integration test binary is prefixed by its surface and selected into its layer by that prefix; test functions follow the naming rule; shared helpers are reused, never copied
each new test creates its own private home, seeds its own data, and produces on-disk product state by running viola, never by hand-writing it
each new test runs and revives under a test-owned user home and runtime dir, its home under the one test-home root
each new test asserts literal oracles on the contract, uses no sleep or retry, no process-wide env mutation, no shared mutable state, and runs in parallel
each new fake or double is a real stub executable or a seam trait, never a mock of what is not owned, and nothing is mocked in E2E
new code counts toward the comprehensive-tier coverage floors and the mutation gate at the epoch boundary; no #[ignore] parking
each new process log line is one JSON object per line through the tracing subscriber, with the harness-grepped fields and corr where defined
each OS- or host-gated test is registered with its reason and kept in the binary's root file

Absences of Windows and macOS support, a database, outbound HTTP, a browser suite and a deploy stage: nothing of the chunk touches them.
